options: It calculates depreciation for each asset
It creates new asset categories
It transfers journal entries into Payables
It generates subledger journal entries from Assets transactions like additions, depreciation, and retirements
questions.explain: Create Accounting reads Assets transactions and generates the actual journal entries representing them, using the Subledger Accounting engine.

questions.q: Which accounts does a typical depreciation run's journal entry affect?
options: Asset cost and asset clearing
Depreciation expense and accumulated depreciation
Revaluation reserve and gain on retirement
Accounts payable and accounts receivable
questions.explain: A depreciation run debits depreciation expense and credits accumulated depreciation for every successfully calculated asset.

questions.q: What is the difference between draft and final accounting in Create Accounting?
options: There is no difference between the two
Draft mode only applies to tax books
Final mode is only used during asset retirement
Draft generates entries for review without posting them; final commits the entries, making them eligible to transfer to GL
questions.explain: Draft accounting lets someone review generated journal entries before they are committed; final accounting commits them for transfer to the General Ledger.

questions.q: Where do the default accounts used by Create Accounting ultimately come from?
options: They are entered manually on every single transaction
The General Ledger's chart of accounts, unrelated to Assets setup
They are randomly assigned by the system
The default accounts set up in category books back in Chapter 2
questions.explain: Create Accounting relies on the default cost, clearing, expense, and reserve accounts configured in category books, making that earlier setup critical to accurate accounting.

questions.q: Why is Create Accounting described as a bridge between Assets and the General Ledger?
options: Because it deletes all detail once journal entries are created
Because it only runs once per year
Because it replaces the need for a General Ledger entirely
Because it summarizes Assets' detailed transactional data into account-level journal entries that GL needs
questions.explain: Assets keeps far more detail (asset numbers, locations, categories) than GL requires; Create Accounting summarizes that detail into the account-level entries GL actually uses.
